About the role As part of a high-performing legal team, you will work at the centre of major infrastructure projects and broader commercial strategy. This is not a traditional legal advisory role. You will work closely with commercial, finance, development and project teams throughout the lifecycle of significant infrastructure projects, providing practical legal and commercial advice on complex transactions and project arrangements. You will: Advise on the legal and commercial frameworks supporting major infrastructure projects, including PPPs and other government-backed projects. Support the development, financing and delivery of significant infrastructure opportunities. Work closely with internal commercial, finance, development and project teams, as well as external advisers and project stakeholders. Advise on project and construction documentation, including project deeds, development arrangements, delivery agreements and other major contracts. Assist with the identification, negotiation and allocation of legal and commercial risk throughout the project lifecycle. Provide strategic advice on contractual, corporate, governance and regulatory matters affecting projects and the broader business. Support ongoing compliance with contractual obligations and applicable governance and sustainability requirements. About you This role will suit an experienced projects, infrastructure or construction lawyer who is looking to move in-house, or an existing in-house lawyer seeking greater exposure to major projects and commercial decision-making. You will ideally possess: 8+ years' PQE. Experience across infrastructure, major projects, PPPs, project finance and/or construction. Strong experience reviewing and negotiating complex project and commercial agreements. An understanding of project delivery models and the allocation of risk across major infrastructure projects. The ability to look beyond the legal position and understand the broader commercial drivers of a project. Superior communication, influencing and negotiation skills. A proactive, solutions-focused and pragmatic approach. This is an excellent opportunity for a lawyer who wants to play a central role in major infrastructure projects and work closely with senior commercial stakeholders on strategically important transactions. To Apply If you're interested in learning more about this opportunity, contact Nathan Aron , Associate Director, on 0419 511 439 for a confidential discussion. Alternatively, send your CV to nathan@sigmaexecutive.com.au.

review_candidates.title: Senior Dams Engineer
review_candidates.description: Job Description At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day. That’s why we pledge to support and empower all of our people to make a positive impact when working hand in hand with our business to drive change. We'll help you accelerate your career and empower you with the right technology and training as you bring ideas and projects to life. Together with your colleagues, clients and partners, you'll make an impact that is felt by all. See where your commitment could take you. Who are we looking for? We are seeking an experienced Senior Dams Engineer to join our nationally connected Dams and Tailings team for NSW/ACT, to be based in our Sydney (St Leonards), Canberra, Newcastle or Wollongong office. This is an opportunity to contribute to some of Australia’s most significant dam design, upgrade and safety projects, applying your technical expertise to complex engineering challenges across major dams, spillways, embankments and associated water infrastructure. Working alongside industry-leading specialists, you’ll play a key role in delivering practical and technically robust solutions, fostering client relationships and mentoring junior engineers, and this role offers the chance to further develop your technical and leadership capabilities in a collaborative, supportive environment. Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in: The design, assessment and safety evaluation of concrete and embankment dams, spillways, outlet works and associated water infrastructure. Delivery of dam-related projects across the full lifecycle, from feasibility and concept development through to detailed design and construction support. Undertaking dam safety surveillance, risk assessments and mitigation planning for major dam owners. Coordinating multidisciplinary teams and collaborating with geotechnical, structural, hydraulic and environmental specialists to deliver integrated solutions. Building strong client, regulator and stakeholder relationships while contributing to proposals and business development activities. Managing project budgets, schedules and delivery outcomes while mentoring junior engineers and supporting capability growth across the dams team. What you will bring to the team: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline, with 7+ years’ experience in dams and or tailings engineering, ideally within a consulting environment. Demonstrated experience in the design, assessment and delivery of dams, associated water infrastructure or tailings projects. Experience delivering projects from concept through to detailed design, construction support and project close-out. Strong understanding of ANCOLD guidelines, dam safety principles and relevant engineering standards. Excellent project management, problem-solving, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams, with Chartered status or progress towards Chartership highly regarded. Interested? Apply online now by submitting your CV and Cover Letter. GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities. GHD embraces hybrid work arrangements to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive. This supports the diverse needs of our workforce while balancing the benefits of remote working with the value of face-to-face collaboration in the office. We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage. About Us Come together and make a meaningful impact. We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD. Let's drive real change. Our Pledge to You At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day. That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today. See where your commitment could take you. That’s the #PowerOfCommitment Who We Are GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents. The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

review_candidates.title: Reticulation Construction Manager - Wind Energy | Electrical Infrastructure
review_candidates.description: Reticulation Construction Manager Wind Energy | Electrical Infrastructure | Build a New Delivery Capability Brisbane / North Queensland | Major Renewable Energy Project This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage construction from behind a desk. We're looking for an experienced Reticulation Construction Manager to take ownership of a major underground electrical reticulation scope on one of Queensland's significant new renewable energy projects. More importantly, you'll have the opportunity to help build an internal reticulation capability from the ground up for a growing Australian electrical infrastructure contractor. The business is investing significantly in its own specialist plant and equipment, people and self-perform capability. They need someone who genuinely understands how to put the operation together and make it productive. The opportunity Initially, you'll take responsibility for establishing and delivering the underground reticulation construction capability for a major wind project in North Queensland. You'll be responsible for: Mobilising and establishing the reticulation construction operation Managing electrical reticulation crews and supervisors Setting up and operating specialist cable installation equipment Driving productivity, utilisation and output Planning labour, plant, equipment and construction sequencing Cable drum, pulling and installation planning Coordinating trenching, cable installation, jointing and termination activities Managing equipment servicing, maintenance and availability Establishing practical construction methodologies and processes Working closely with engineering, project management, commercial and project controls Managing interfaces with other construction disciplines and subcontractors Building a safe, repeatable and scalable delivery model You'll have strong commercial and project support around you. We're not looking for an accountant with construction experience — we're looking for someone who knows how to physically deliver this work. Longer term The ambition is bigger than one project. The business wants to increase the amount of electrical construction it self-performs across its renewable energy portfolio. For the right person, this is an opportunity to take what you establish on the first project and help develop it into a reticulation service line capable of supporting future projects nationally. If you're currently running reticulation crews for another contractor and wondering what the next step looks like, this could be it. You'll ideally bring experience across: Underground HV/MV electrical reticulation Wind farm collection systems or similar large-scale electrical infrastructure Cable installation, pulling, jointing and terminations Specialist cable installation plant and equipment Managing crews in a self-perform environment Construction planning and mobilisation Plant utilisation and productivity High-risk construction environments Managing multiple workfronts Building and developing construction teams Experience with wind farms and 33kV collection systems would be particularly attractive. We're interested in an excellent Construction Manager, Reticulation Manager, Superintendent or Operations Manager who has the technical knowledge, leadership ability and ambition to step up and help build something. Why consider it? This is a rare opportunity to join a growing electrical infrastructure contractor at the point where they're making a deliberate move towards greater self-performance. Rather than inheriting an established operation, you'll have genuine input into how the crews are structured, how the equipment is deployed, how productivity is achieved and ultimately how the capability grows. If you know underground electrical reticulation inside out and want the opportunity to build rather than simply maintain, I'd like to hear from you.

review_candidates.description: About The Job Responsible for planning, designing, implementing, and reporting for Real-World Evidence (RWE) and Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) studies. The person in this role will also contribute to face-to-face client meetings, teleconference calls, study design, reporting and publication strategies. RWE clinical study scope includes both prospective and retrospective site-based studies, pragmatic trials, decentralized trials, existing secondary data only studies as well as HEOR projects, including literature reviews, meta-analyses, and medical writing activities What You'll Do: Develop Real-World Evidence study protocols/analysis plans, clinical study reports, abstracts and manuscripts ensuring quality and completeness of client deliverables. Lead the conduct of systematic literature reviews and meta-analyses Lead studies involving health economics and outcomes research, including patient/provider perspective, patient reported outcomes measures (PROMs), and cost/benefit analyses Lead studies utilizing existing secondary data sources (e.g., registries, medical claims, electronic healthcare records). Includes programming requirements, analysis and final reporting writing. Interact with clients and team members to determine real-world evidence (RWE) or health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) needs, objectives, and project scope. Participate in internal and client launch meetings to understand the project background, study requirements, timelines and deliverables. Identify appropriate literature, data sources and tools for research to meet client needs. Distill input from clients, clinicians, medical coders, existing data and published literature to assist in the overall study design. Provide epidemiologic input into the statistical analysis plan and output required to meet study objectives. Responsible for ongoing data review from an epidemiologic standpoint. Prepare for and attend expert panels and advisory boards, assist in collection of information and elaboration of meeting reports. Responsible for interpreting clinical outcomes research results and providing epidemiologic expertise in using the most appropriate statistical analysis methods for each study. Work closely with a statistician in the analysis and reporting of clinical study results Prioritize and manage time effectively to meet the needs of multiple clients. Work within project budgets and complete high-quality deliverables in a timely manner. Assist in developing proposals, including providing input into the scientific rationale, methodology, timelines, and budgets. Collaborate with various CTI departments, based on project or study scope What You'll Bring: At least 3 years’ experience in working in outcomes research and/or epidemiology. Master’s degree in public health, epidemiology, health services research, pharmacy, nursing, natural science, biostatistics, or closely related discipline About CTI CTI Clinical Trial and Consulting Services is a global, privately held, full-service clinical contract research organization (CRO) focused on the advancement of treatments for chronically and critically ill patient populations. We assist clinical research throughout the lifecycle of development, from drug concept to commercialization. CTI is headquartered in the Greater Cincinnati, OH region with global operations in collaboration with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device firms. For more information, visit www.ctifacts.com Why CTI? Advance Your Career – We support career progression through a structured mentoring program and leadership courses that provide the support needed to grow. We also value ongoing education and training through tuition reimbursement and a dedicated training department. Join an Award-Winning and Valued Team – We have an award-winning unparalleled culture that can be felt by our employees across 60 countries. We support a work-life balance and the importance of time with family by offering generous health benefits and vacation packages, hybrid work from home opportunities, and paid parental leave. Make a Lasting Impact – We focus on moving medicine forward by working on treatments for chronically and critically-ill patients, who depend on us to bring life-changing therapies to market. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated experience developing and executing integrated public policy, advocacy, or government relations campaigns. review_candidates.title: Programme Development Lead - Predator Free in Tāmaki Makaurau
review_candidates.description: Programme Development Lead - Predator Free in Tāmaki Makaurau Organisation: NEXT Foundation Location: Auckland, full time, in person & field work Contract: 12-month fixed-term Salary: NZD $150,000–$200,000 pa depending on experience About NEXT Foundation NEXT Foundation is a strategic philanthropy fund applying business rigour to giving, to help inspire the world’s first Nature Positive country. It has catalysed programmes including Predator Free Wellington and Zero Invasive Predators and brings direct experience scaling predator-free efforts from concept to operational delivery. About the opportunity Auckland is already a national leader in predator control and island eradication, with a track record stretching back more than sixty years - from the open sanctuary on Tiritiri Matangi and community pioneers such as Ark in the Park, to a Hauraki Gulf that now holds more than 30 predator-free islands and a mainland network of 500-plus active community groups. It is now time to build on that momentum and explore the potential to go after a bold new collective goal: to accelerate Predator Free in Tāmaki Makaurau (PFinTM). PFinTM is a focus area of the Nature Positive Auckland ambition and a key part of the national Predator Free 2050 programme. As New Zealand’s largest city and the gateway to the Hauraki Gulf, Auckland is both the greatest challenge and the greatest opportunity in the country’s predator-free journey - the place that could connect mainland and island gains and show that elimination is achievable in a major city. PFinTM’s purpose would be to amplify and coordinate the huge effort already underway and build a shared delivery model to enable predator elimination to happen at-scale in the region. Before a programme can be stood up, scoping and planning work is needed to figure out what a PFinTM programme could look like - including initial mana whenua and community engagement, technical feasibility, sequencing, partnership, governance, and funding considerations. This role would lead that initial engagement and technical planning and scoping work, taking ownership of shaping what a potential large-scale programme could become. Key Responsibilities -          Project ownership o  Take ownership of an emerging initiative to build the case, relationships and design needed to turn a bold ambition into a real, fundable programme. -          Planning and technical leadership o  Lead and integrate the workstreams that produce the draft PFinTM implementation plan, to time and budget o  Bring technical rigour to elimination feasibility, zone design, operational sequencing, tool selection, and costing - drawing on urban and landscape-scale elimination experience o  Coordinate inputs from the specialist GIS and ecology team and partner liaisons to translate technical analysis into clear options for partners -          Mana whenua and community engagement o  Lead early engagement with mana whenua and community conservation networks o  Uphold tikanga and work respectfully across Auckland’s mana whenua landscape o  Shape a proposed engagement approach and sequencing for the deeper, at-place engagement a potential future programme would require -          Partnership, coordination and reporting o  Work in close partnership with Auckland Council, DOC, and NEXT Foundation and report to the project’s steering / oversight arrangements About you This role would be well-suited for a relationally minded leader, with a technical background in predator management and project planning, who is skilled at championing a bold region-wide vision. Essential skills and experience ●        Ability to champion a vision and build region-wide buy-in, including influencing partners and funders, and articulating a value proposition for the project that reaches all Aucklanders ●        Strong working knowledge of predator management, including methods, tools and operational design across urban and/or landscape-scale contexts ●        Community and mana whenua engagement experience , including a demonstrated ability to engage with Te Ao Māori and tikanga Māori, and to build trust across diverse communities ●        Ownership and initiative - an entrepreneurial, self-directed operator who can build a role and shape an early-stage ambition into a fundable programme ●        Strong planning, feasibility, and operational-design skills , including sequencing, risk, costing, and options analysis ●        Excellent stakeholder and partnership skills across government, philanthropy, iwi, and community ●        Sound budget, project-management and reporting discipline Desirable skills and experience ●       Existing understanding of and relationships with Tāmaki Makaurau’s mana whenua and community ecosystems ●       Experience with Predator Free 2050 programmes or comparable large-scale conservation initiatives ●       Competency with GIS-based spatial planning tools How to apply Send your CV and a cover letter outlining what draws you to this opportunity and your relevant experience to deb.turton@nextfoundation.org.nz by Friday 9 October 2026.
